I am 76 years old, and I have worked the land in Quzhou County since I was a young boy. I only went to primary school, but this soil has been my real teacher for over sixty years. Here on the North China Plain, the only sensible thing to do is what my father did and what my neighbors still do: plant winter wheat in the autumn, harvest it in early summer, and immediately follow it with summer maize. My wheat is already in the ground from last October. Now that spring has come, I will top-dress it with urea and irrigate it three or four times before harvest. I buy improved wheat seeds and hybrid maize seeds from the township supply store because they are reliable and the corn grows fast enough to finish before autumn cold. I keep four mu of land — at my age, that is all my legs and back can handle, though my son helps me at harvest time. I apply plenty of nitrogen because our soil is tired after so many years of cropping, along with some phosphate and potash. I spray pesticides when I see aphids or rust, usually two or three times a season. I plough the ground before wheat and use the rotary tiller before maize. I do not experiment with vegetables or orchards; wheat and maize feed my household and leave enough grain to sell for cash. I expect fair yields if the rain and the pumps do their part.
